description:
Form: pick
Header: Pick work

Context:
- Your open beads hold four items from June. One is already done (PR #1, the Markdown timeline export, is merged). One is obsolete: both clippy warnings sit in code that upstream has since rewritten. That leaves the three options below.
- Option a evidence: on 2026-06-07 you wrote 'There's been a lot of progress it looks like on this since I forked. Please pull the changes from the upstream repo and reconcile.' A session merged 285 upstream commits and opened PR #2, but PR #2 was never merged. Upstream has since added 217 more commits and released 4.2, 4.3 and 5.0.1.
- Option a plan, step 1: build PR #2 on today's Rust and run its tests, then merge it into develop (this fork's main branch). A dry-run merge into develop shows no conflicts. Step 2: merge the 217 newer upstream commits, fix 5 conflicting files (2 real: the CLI options file and the HTML stylesheet), and re-check the timeline export and -w against upstream 5.0. Step 2 may still be in progress at 3 pm.
- Option b evidence: on 2026-05-10 you wrote 'I don't think the issue is full disk access -- I can access the chat.db file from the terminal.' The cause was that macOS checks the built binary itself, not the terminal. The message still says to give your terminal Full Disk Access, in this fork and in upstream today.
- Option c evidence is weaker: a Claude session wrote this bead on 2026-06-07 when you asked it to 'file beads for the remaining items'. Your own words never named link previews or music. Today the timeline export prints '[App message]' for link previews, Apple Music shares, polls and similar messages.
- Safety: players test only on the repo's test fixtures and on a copy of chat.db inside the repo's tmp folder (git-ignored and in your Dropbox ignore list). They check exit codes and file counts only, and never read message text, so no message content goes to the model or off this Mac.
- How you test option a: copy the database with cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db* /tmp/imx/ and run the new binary with -p /tmp/imx/chat.db -f timeline -w on one contact. I will give exact commands when it is built. Your daily imessage-exporter is still Homebrew 3.3.2 from February, which has no timeline format.

Options:
a. (Recommended) Land the upstream sync: merge PR #2 now, then bring in upstream 5.0.1. Upside: finishes your June request and picks up 5 months of upstream fixes. Downside: biggest change, about 60 to 75 minutes, and step 2 may not finish before 3 pm.
b. Fix the Full Disk Access error message: name the binary path to add, and suggest -p with a copied database. Upside: about 15 minutes, fixes the exact confusion you hit. Downside: small. Best done after option a, because upstream rewrote that file.
c. Render link previews, music and polls in the timeline export instead of [App message]. Upside: richer exports. Downside: about 45 to 60 minutes, depends on option a landing first, and the evidence you want it is weak. I would not start it before 3 pm.

No default: the session stops here

title: Richer Timeline balloon rendering
description: Wire URL/Music/Poll/Collaboration/Edited/Sticker balloon types in the Timeline exporter. Currently all BubbleComponent::App variants fall through to msg.text or '[App message]'. Parity with TXT for at least URL previews and music messages would be the v1 target.

title: Improve FDA error message
description: In data_source.rs, when sqlite returns 'unable to open database file', the current hint tells the user to grant FDA to their terminal — but on macOS Sequoia+, the built binary itself needs FDA, not the terminal. Sharpen the hint to name the binary path explicitly.
